hypotheses.name: Cloud Buffering
hypotheses.statement: Earth's globally-averaged albedo maintains its stability and symmetry through cloud buffering: clouds scattering compensates variations in surface albedo and aerosols that would otherwise impact albedo.
hypotheses.source: Stephens et al. (2015); Feldman et al. (2026) Nature paper

testable_predictions.prediction: Cloud area fraction inversely and causally responds to surface albedo perturbations
testable_predictions.current_result: correlational support (FFNN perturbation shows inverse response)

testable_predictions.prediction: After volcanic AOD increases, cloud radiative effects decrease to partially compensate
testable_predictions.needs: formal statistical test using Pinatubo as natural experiment

testable_predictions.prediction: Hemispheric cloud response is asymmetric to cross-hemisphere perturbations
Cloud buffering is stronger over oceans (marine boundary layer) than over land

history.rationale: Prior FFNN perturbation work provides correlational support; causal evidence needed

hypotheses.name: Invariant Earth System Properties
hypotheses.statement: Earth's TOA albedo stability and hemispheric symmetry result from properties of the Earth system at the surface and in the troposphere that are invariant on 21st Century timescales (physical constants, geometry, water optical properties).

testable_predictions.prediction: Physical constants (Clausius-Clapeyron, water optics, geometry) analytically constrain albedo to the observed ~29% range
testable_predictions.needs: analytical derivation + comparison with observed range

testable_predictions.prediction: Invariant-linked features (lat, lon, month) explain >60% of albedo variance
testable_predictions.needs: partition features into invariant vs variable groups

testable_predictions.prediction: Removing latitude from FFNN causes disproportionate degradation (>3x vs any cloud variable)
testable_predictions.current_result: U-Net ablation shows latitude removal causes large RMSE increase
testable_predictions.needs: formal FFNN ablation with statistical comparison

history.rationale: SHAP shows latitude importance but no formal invariant properties test conducted

hypotheses.name: Teleconnections
hypotheses.statement: Hemispheric albedo symmetry is maintained by spatial teleconnections — cross-regional and cross-hemispheric correlations in cloud, aerosol, and surface albedo fields that actively couple distant regions.
hypotheses.source: Feldman et al. (2026) Nature paper; U-Net analysis

testable_predictions.prediction: NH-mean and SH-mean albedo anomaly time series are significantly correlated
Spatial correlation maps reveal 3+ 'control regions' with r>0.3 to global mean
testable_predictions.current_result: U-Net found no discernible regional control structure
testable_predictions.needs: network-based analysis may reveal distributed (not localized) control

testable_predictions.prediction: Lagged correlations between regional albedo anomalies reveal energy transport pathways
Seasonal vs interannual teleconnection structures differ
testable_predictions.needs: separate seasonal cycle from interannual variability

history.rationale: U-Net showed no regional control; but network methods may reveal distributed teleconnections
